plan: Sell all leveraged ETFs (SOXL, SPAL, MUU, PLTU) to zero to reduce volatility.
Exit high-beta software names (METU, MSFU) for capital preservation.
Trim the income ETF (QQQI) to 20% to meet concentration limits.
Hold remaining broad index and quality tech positions.
This plan prioritizes reducing risk and building a cash buffer.
Focus is on capital preservation with minimal drawdown.
conservative.read: This conservative approach aims for lower monthly gains, likely around 1-2%, by significantly reducing leverage and volatile assets. The primary goal is capital preservation, accepting lower upside potential for a much lower risk of substantial losses.

plan: Trim leveraged ETFs (SOXL, MUU, SPAL) and high-beta software (METU, MSFU) to small positions.
Introduce a new, high-quality scanner setup (VRT) at 4% to add growth potential.
Maintain exposure to broad indices and remaining tech holdings.
This plan balances risk reduction with targeted growth opportunities.
It aims for steady, risk-managed gains by trimming weaker areas and adding strength.
Cash buffer will increase slightly as volatile assets are reduced.
balanced.read: This balanced plan targets around 2-3% monthly gains by reducing exposure to the riskiest assets and adding a promising new name. It seeks growth while keeping risk in check, aiming for a smoother equity curve than aggressive strategies.

plan: Increase exposure to leveraged ETFs (SOXL, MUU, SPAL) and high-beta software (METU, MSFU) to 6% each.
Add a new, high-quality scanner setup (VRT) at 6% to capture upside.
This plan concentrates capital in high-conviction, high-beta areas.
It aims for aggressive growth by leveraging strong trends and potential upside.
Expect higher volatility and larger potential drawdowns.
Strict stop-loss discipline is critical to manage risk.
aggressive.read: This aggressive plan targets 4%+ monthly gains by concentrating capital in leveraged ETFs and high-beta tech, plus adding a strong new setup. It embraces higher risk for potentially higher reward, but this also means significantly larger drawdowns are possible, especially with leverage and daily rebalancing of leveraged ETFs.

plan: Sell all leveraged ETFs (SOXL, MUU, SPAL) and high-beta software (METU, MSFU) to zero.
Increase allocation to the income ETF (QQQI) to 30% for monthly distributions.
This plan prioritizes generating steady income over capital appreciation.
It aims for low drawdowns and reliable, though variable, monthly payouts.
Remaining capital will be held in broad index ETFs for stability.
This strategy is designed for capital preservation with yield.
income.read: This income-focused plan targets around 1% monthly in distributions by shifting heavily into income-generating ETFs like QQQI. It significantly reduces risk and volatility, prioritizing steady cash flow over growth. While distributions are the goal, the Net Asset Value can still decline in market downturns.
